subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation exact-host allowlist entries continue to allow non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback after the trusted-host SSRF tightening?
rationale: Preserving the old browser test restores an operator-declared exception, while retiring it keeps the newly accepted SSRF protection against trusted-host loopback rebinding; automation should not choose that security boundary.

options.title: Retire the old loopback-alias contract
options.body: Keep the hardened trusted-host behavior and update the browser navigation test/docs to require localhost, loopback literals, or explicit private-network opt-in.

options.title: Approve a scoped browser exception
options.body: Allow exact browser navigation allowlist entries to override loopback DNS answers only through a narrowly scoped path that preserves metadata/link-local protections.

options.title: Defer to broader SSRF design
options.body: Keep this open until browser, provider, fetch, and CDP SSRF policy semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Retire the old loopback-alias contract
recommendation.body: Keep the hardened trusted-host behavior and update the browser navigation test/docs to require localhost, loopback literals, or explicit private-network opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent signal across the issue, the accepted SSRF hardening, and adjacent browser CDP policy work.
